h: Hitmen, a boxer and a diner robbery shuffled out of order, with talk about burgers and foot massages that is as gripping as the shootouts.

like.t: Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels
like.r: British gangsters and a tangled plot told with the same chatty swagger, faster and cheekier but less interested in redemption.
The crime film Tarantino grew up on: mobsters who talk like real people, with a far more sorrowful view of the life.
Another genre exercise full of bad plans and black humor, tighter and quieter.

h: A jewel heist gone wrong, told through a warehouse full of bleeding men in black suits who suspect one of them is a cop.

like.r: Another crew of criminals and a story you reassemble from fragments, with a more elaborate puzzle at its center.
The Hong Kong undercover-cop thriller that Tarantino borrowed from, with the same loyalty and betrayal among thieves.
The cool, professional-thief heist film in a larger and more melancholy key, with better gunfights.

h: A flight attendant in her forties plays a gunrunner and two federal agents against each other in Tarantino's warmest, most grown-up film.

like.r: The source novel, with the same lived-in crooks and double-crosses on the page, drier and more procedural.
Another Elmore Leonard adaptation with a smart woman across the table from a criminal and a relaxed, funky rhythm.
A crime story where the sharpest person in the room is an unglamorous woman, with a colder sense of humor.

h: Thirty years inside the mob, narrated by a man who loves every perk and sweats through every bill; seductive, hilarious, then frightening.

like.r: The same director, narrators and brutal bookkeeping, swapped from New York streets to the Las Vegas strip.
The grander, more operatic mob saga that Goodfellas deliberately answers with a street-level view.
The nonfiction book the film is based on, with the real Henry Hill's voice and more detail.

h: Money, mobsters and a marriage rot together in Vegas; three hours of excess narrated by the people who think they run it.

like.r: Tighter and more fun, with the same voiceover-driven rise and collapse of men who get greedy.
Another story of a criminal empire that eats its builder, louder and more cartoonish than Casino.
A similar swooping, music-filled rise-and-fall structure, set in the porn business instead of the casino.

h: Gilded Age New York, where a hand brushing a glove is the whole affair and the rules do the violence that guns do in Scorsese's other films.

like.r: The novel is just as restrained and even sharper on how a society punishes people without raising its voice.
Another story of love lost to propriety and duty, set in an English household.
Also about heartfelt feeling squeezed by class and etiquette, but lighter and more hopeful.

h: A profiteer in occupied Poland slowly turns into a rescuer, shot in stark black and white that makes you feel every minute of its three hours.

like.r: The novelistic account the film is adapted from, richer on the survivors and the odd, vain man who saved them.
Another Holocaust story of survival in Poland, narrower and more personal, with a quieter style.
Spielberg's other war film, with a similar shocking realism, set on the battlefield instead of in the ghettos.

h: A theme park of cloned dinosaurs goes wrong in the dark; sheer wonder at the first sight of them, then pure movie terror.

like.r: The novel is meaner and more scientific, with chaos theory, a darker corporate story and more bodies.
The earlier, simpler Spielberg monster picture, scarier because it shows less of the creature.
A tense, claustrophobic hunt by a creature that humans foolishly brought along; much darker, with nothing playful in it.

h: A harrowing Normandy landing, then a small squad crossing France to bring one man home; war as chaos, with a sentimental heart.

like.r: Released the same year, a dreamy, philosophical take on combat that turns inward instead of toward the squad.
A grunt's-eye, personal view of war that is just as unsparing, but set in Vietnam and far more cynical.
An immersive, almost wordless war picture that puts you in the middle of the fighting, with less sentiment.

h: An insomniac office drone and a charismatic soap salesman start a basement brawling club, then it gets away from them in nasty ways.

like.r: The novel is leaner, meaner and weirder, with the same narrator voice and a slightly different ending.
Another satire of male consumer culture narrated by a man who can't feel anything, much more repellent.
The original lonely, insomniac, angry narrator spiraling toward violence, grimier and less ironic.

h: Two detectives, one weary and one eager, chase a killer staging murders around the seven deadly sins in a rain-soaked city; it ends badly.

like.r: Another serial-killer hunt with a brilliant, unnerving villain, with a bit more humanity and less despair.
Fincher on a real unsolved case, slower and drier, about the obsession with finding a killer.
A grim, darkly funny serial-killer investigation that is also about the failure of the detectives.

h: A rich, cold banker gets a birthday gift: an elaborate game that starts to dismantle his life, and he can't tell what is real.

like.r: Fincher's next film, with the same protagonist who needs his life stripped away, bolder and angrier.
Another man manipulated by an unseen designer, gentler and more satirical, with a wide, sunny look.
A paranoid thriller in which the people around the hero may all be in on it, as slow and creepy as The Game is slick.

h: A botched kidnapping across snowy Minnesota, with a polite, pregnant police chief who is the only person who seems to think straight.

like.r: The Coens' bleaker, quieter crime story, with a relentless killer and a weary lawman instead of laughs.
Their first film, a stripped-down tale of an ordinary scheme going wrong, darker and less amiable.
Another snowbound story of ordinary people corrupted by money, with fewer jokes and a grimmer arc.

h: A deeply relaxed slacker is dragged into a kidnapping plot by a stolen rug, and bowling remains more important than all of it.

like.r: The shaggy-detective prototype the Coens riff on, with a lost-in-Los-Angeles hero, played far straighter.
Another stoned detective story in which the case is incoherent and the mood is the point.
Earlier Coens screwball with the same eccentric dialogue and cartoonish mishaps.

h: A gangster's cool adviser plays two Prohibition-era bosses against each other in a story of loyalty, hats and heartless talk.

like.r: The hardboiled novel the film borrows from, with the same machinations and an unsentimental political boss.
A far bigger and more operatic gangster saga with a similar focus on loyalty and cold decisions.
Another stylish, fatalistic story of corruption, with a detective who is outmatched.

h: A high-minded New York playwright is stuck with writer's block in a sweaty Hollywood hotel, and the building gets stranger than his scripts.

like.r: Hollywood chewing up a writer, in a classic noir that is much more straightforward.
Another nightmare about the movie business whose logic slips away, even more mysterious and more erotic.
A comic, anxious portrait of a screenwriter with a block, with similar self-loathing and meta humor.

h: A hacker learns his world is a simulation and gets taught to bend its rules in kung-fu fights that changed how action looks.

like.r: The cyberpunk novel that set up the vocabulary of jacking into cyberspace, bleaker and far more hard-boiled.
A moodier, slower meditation on what is real and what is human in a neon-lit future.
The anime that heavily inspired the Wachowskis, more philosophical and quiet about minds in machines.

h: An ex-con plumber and a mobster's girlfriend fall for each other and plan to steal two million dollars, in a neo-noir shot with high style.

like.r: A neo-noir with the same love for a scheme that unravels in small, sweaty, escalating mistakes.
Another glossy, sexy thriller with a dangerous woman, trashier and louder.
The classic noir of lovers who plot a crime together, told with a sharp fatalism.

h: A busboy with one gift joins a family of porn-industry oddballs in the Valley; a joyous sprawl that darkens as the disco ends.

like.r: Anderson's next ensemble, with the same Valley, the same cast, and bigger, rawer swings at grief.
The roving camera, needle-drops and rise-and-fall shape Anderson was echoing, applied to the mob.
Another 1970s coming-of-age in a surrogate family of hustlers, with more warmth and less despair.

h: A dozen lonely San Fernando Valley lives collide over a single day, building to an outrageous and oddly moving moment of release.

like.r: The Los Angeles mosaic that Magnolia learns from, with more dry observation and less operatic pain.
The same director's earlier ensemble, more playful and period-driven, with a gentler path.
Another interlocking Los Angeles ensemble, more issue-driven and neat than Magnolia.

h: An overachieving, underperforming prep-school kid fights a millionaire for the affections of a teacher, in a meticulous, bittersweet comedy.

like.r: Anderson's next film, with the same dollhouse style, more characters and a larger sadness.
The offbeat, deadpan romance between mismatched people that Anderson's tone owes a lot to.
Another story of a young man's confused love for an older woman, set to a famous soundtrack.

h: Three gentle dreamers plan a robbery with a binder full of schemes; a small, sweet crime comedy before the Wes Anderson look took over.

like.r: Anderson's follow-up, with the same wry affection, more polished and more heartfelt.
Another loose, quotable hangout film about aimless friends, in the high-school 1970s.
Another 1996 debut about small-time characters in a modest crime story, quieter and sadder.

h: The last day of school in 1976 Texas stretches into a long night of hazing, beer and classic rock, with no real plot and all the vibe.

like.r: The original one-night-in-the-past teen movie with a jukebox soundtrack, a bit sweeter.
A raunchier and more episodic high-school ensemble from the same sort of hangout tradition.
Linklater's later, quieter look at growing up, filmed over twelve years.

h: Two strangers get off a train in Vienna and talk until dawn; a whole love story made of walking, wandering and unguarded conversation.

like.r: Another brief, wistful connection between two lonely people in a foreign city, quieter and more melancholy.
The classic of a short, intense meeting between two people, with a restrained English ache.
Another small, spontaneous romance between two strangers, this time carried by songs.

h: A young FBI trainee trades secrets with an imprisoned genius cannibal to catch a killer, in a chilling duel of wits.

like.r: The novel is just as tense, with more procedure, more of Clarice's inner life and a nastier tone.
A bleaker serial-killer hunt with a rain-soaked look and no uplift.
The first screen version of Hannibal Lecter, cooler and more stylized, about a profiler who thinks too much like his target.

h: A lawyer fired for having AIDS hires a homophobic rival to sue his firm; a mainstream courtroom drama with a big heart.

like.r: Another earnest, humane drama about prejudice and the law, built on a death penalty case.
A courtroom drama with the same polished star-driven feel, more about military honor than prejudice.
The older lawyer-defends-the-outcast classic that Philadelphia echoes, with a Southern setting.

h: An aging killer takes one last bounty job, and the western myth slowly rots in his hands; violence here costs something.

like.r: The classic western about a haunted, obsessive man that Eastwood questions by looking at its violence honestly.
Another elegy for outlaws too old for the changing West, bloodier and less reflective.
A later western with a gruff, aging gunman, funnier and more traditional.

h: A master thief and an obsessed detective, both brilliant and both lonely, circle each other across a long, sleek Los Angeles night.

like.r: Mann's other night-time Los Angeles thriller, shorter and sleeker, with a hitman in the back of a cab.
Another cops-and-criminals mirror image with a star cast, louder and angrier.
A superhero blockbuster that borrowed Heat's sleek urban crime texture and the cop-against-mastermind duel.

h: A reprogrammed killer robot protects a boy from a liquid-metal assassin; a huge action movie with a surprising heart.

like.r: Cameron's other sequel that outdid its original, with a tough heroine, a gun-heavy plot and a mother's fury.
The model for the decade's action blockbusters, more grounded and wisecracking.
A nonstop practical-effects chase film with a fierce woman at its center, even leaner and more extreme.

h: A rich girl and a penniless artist fall in love on the doomed liner; a huge, sincere romance with a disaster set piece that earns its length.

like.r: The older, more documentary account of the same sinking, without the love story, sober and detailed.
Another sweeping, tragic wartime romance told in flashback, with a slower and more literary feel.
A historic upheaval seen through a doomed love triangle, much more political.

h: A kind, slow-witted man drifts through decades of American history, loving one woman who never stays; sentimental, funny and tailor-made for tears.

like.r: The novel is saltier and more satirical, with a Forrest who is much more chaotic.
Another tall-tale life story told with warmth and wonder, more fantastical.
A simple man is mistaken for a sage in a cooler, drier satire of America.

h: A radio astronomer picks up a message from deep space and has to argue science, religion and politics to answer it.

like.r: The novel has more science and philosophy and a wider cast, with the same hope.
Another scientist-heroine first contact that is moodier and more mournful.
The cold, mysterious ancestor of all serious contact films, with far less personal feeling.

h: A gentle artificial man with blades for hands is adopted by a pastel suburb that loves him, then turns on him.

like.r: The original sympathetic creation rejected by society, much darker and more philosophical.
Burton's more chaotic and comic take on misfit weirdness, with fewer tears.
Another satire of a perfect suburb being disrupted by outsiders, with a fantasy conceit.

h: The cheerful worst director in history makes terrible films with a crew of misfits, and Burton shoots him with pure affection.

like.r: Another loving comedy about a sincerely terrible filmmaker and the friend who stays by him.
The harsh, bitter flip side of Hollywood dreaming, as a classic noir.
Another warm tribute to the odd pioneers of early cinema.

h: Two sisters left without money in Regency England, one sensible and one passionate, find love through heartbreak.

like.r: Austen's brighter and sharper comedy of manners, with a more famous romance.
A later, stylized Austen adaptation, funnier and brisker.
Another English period drama about love lost to restraint, sadder and quieter.

h: Two suburban Connecticut families fumble through affairs and key parties in 1973 while their kids stumble through their own, until the weather breaks.

like.r: The novel is more bitterly funny, with a cooler view of the same suburban collapse.
Another portrait of suburban unhappiness, with more dark comedy.
A bleak novel of a suburban marriage coming apart, with the same sadness.

h: A janitor with a gift for mathematics and a fear of everyone is slowly wrung open by a grieving therapist and his loyal friends.

like.r: Another film about a teacher who changes a young person's life, more romantic and more tragic.
A quieter, more serious therapy drama about a young man's pain and a family that can't talk.
A similar mix of genius and damage, wrapped in a road trip and a brotherly bond.

h: Two street hustlers, one narcoleptic and one a rich kid slumming, drift across the Pacific Northwest in a dreamy, Shakespeare-laced road movie.

like.r: An earlier, grittier story of two hustlers with a fragile friendship in a harsh city.
Another American road movie of wanderers and loss, with a similar dreamy, desert quiet.
A later, devastating story of a love that cannot be spoken, in the American West.

h: A charming bank robber and a U.S. marshal share a trunk and a spark, then spend the movie chasing each other.

like.r: Another Elmore Leonard adaptation with quick, funny crooks and a long, patient pace.
The same director's slick, light heist movie with an ensemble cast.
More of Leonard's cool-voiced crime comedy, with a loan shark who wants to be in movies.

h: A mute Scottish pianist and her daughter are shipped to rough New Zealand, where music becomes her only way to speak, and desire her only leverage.

like.r: The classic of ferocious love on wild land, with the same stormy emotion.

like.t: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
like.r: Another period romance about a woman's inner life and gaze, with a restrained cool.
Campion's gentler, tearful period romance about a poet and his neighbor.

h: From hustler to prisoner to minister and leader, Denzel Washington carries a sprawling, angry, searching biography across three hours.

like.r: The source book, in Malcolm's own words, with more of his thinking and fewer scenes.
Lee's tighter, hotter film about racial tension on one Brooklyn block in a single day.
A focused look at another civil-rights leader, sober and more nonviolent.

h: A shoddily shot day at a New Jersey convenience store where two clerks argue about movies, sex and why they are not at work.

like.r: A low-budget, talky portrait of Gen X aimlessness, more experimental.
Another comedy of hating a dead-end job, with a more polished sheen.
A loose, hanging-out comedy with a similar casual realism and pop-culture talk.

h: A comic-book artist falls for a lesbian friend, and a vulgar, talky romcom turns into an argument about jealousy and honesty.

like.r: The classic can-men-and-women-be-friends romantic comedy, sunnier and more polished.
The neurotic, chatty New York relationship comedy that Smith's talky style borrows from.
Smith's earlier, cruder and funnier film with the same recurring characters and dialogue.

h: Edinburgh heroin addicts narrated with scabrous humor and a thumping soundtrack; exhilarating on the way up and horrible on the way down.

like.r: The novel is written in thick Scots dialect, with more characters and an even rougher voice.
Another stylized, darkly comic film about violent youth culture and a charming narrator.
A far bleaker and more frantic look at addiction, with none of the laughs.

h: Three Edinburgh flatmates find their new lodger dead beside a suitcase of cash and decide to keep it, which ruins everyone.

like.r: Ordinary people destroyed by a pile of money they decide to keep, set in the snow, with more gloom.
A darkly comic crime story in which small greed spirals, quieter and more polite.
Boyle's next film, with the same Scottish sharpness and punk energy, and a bigger reputation.

h: A deadened suburban dad quits his job and starts living again, and the tidy lives around him unravel; black comedy narrated from beyond.

like.r: Another look under the surface of the suburbs, colder and more tragic, set in the 1970s.
The classic novel of suburban disillusion, far more painful and less ironic.
Another 1999 story about an office drone breaking out of a numb life, but violent and more furious.

h: A sour weatherman relives the same day in a small town over and over, and learns to become a better person one loop at a time.

like.r: A modern time-loop romcom, sillier and more romantic, with two people trapped.
The same loop recast as sci-fi action, where each death is a lesson.
The classic of a man who learns his own worth, much more sentimental and old-fashioned.

h: A boy left behind at Christmas defends the house against two burglars with elaborate booby traps; slapstick and holiday sweetness.

like.r: Another suburban kid outsmarting the adults, with a cooler, more teenage attitude.
Another Christmas comedy people rewatch every December, more whimsical.
Columbus's other big family comedy, with more heart about divorce and more manic comedy.

h: A Hollywood Boulevard escort is hired for a week by a cold financier, and the fairy tale predictably, pleasingly happens.

like.r: The classic, charming fairy-tale romance across class lines, more wistful in its ending.
The Pygmalion story of a woman remade for high society, set to song.
Another star-meets-ordinary-person romcom, with a very British, self-deprecating hero.

h: A widower's son calls a radio show, and a woman across the country becomes convinced fate is calling; a romcom that barely lets them meet.

like.r: The old Hollywood weepie that the characters themselves cry over, grander and more tragic.
Ephron's wittier script about friends who fall for each other, funnier and more talky.
Ephron's follow-up with the same stars and another long-distance courtship, with e-mail.

h: A bumbling Englishman keeps meeting an American woman at other people's weddings; shy, clever, with a sudden turn at the funeral.

like.r: Written by the same screenwriter, with the same stammering charm and a more sentimental star romance.
A sprawling, sweeter British ensemble romcom from the same writer.
Another very British, funny and awkward look at love and friends in London, in diary form.

h: A shy London bookseller falls for the world's biggest film star; a polite, self-mocking fairy tale.

like.r: The model for a royal or star falling for an ordinary person, with a gentler, bittersweet ending.
Same writer and lead actor, wittier and a bit sadder, with a bigger ensemble.
Another beloved fairy-tale romance across a gap in wealth and status, glossier and American.

h: A rich Beverly Hills teenager plays matchmaker with total confidence and no idea; a loose Emma with its own slang.

like.r: The source novel, with the same well-meaning matchmaker, in a very different Regency world.
A later and meaner high-school comedy that Clueless paved the way for, with more social warfare.
The pitch-black satire of teen cliques, far nastier.

h: A bad boy is paid to date the school's hardest, most opinionated girl, in a witty, grungy teen update of The Taming of the Shrew.

like.r: Another teen retelling of a classic, with a lighter, glossier tone.
Another turn-of-the-millennium teen romcom with a makeover and a bet.
A later, sharp-tongued high-school comedy with a heroine in control, built on a classic text.

h: A slick sports agent gets fired for a conscience attack and starts over with one client and one loyal accountant.

like.r: Crowe's more personal, music-filled story of a young person finding his way, a bit warmer.
Another sports-business drama about an insider who rethinks everything, drier and more analytical.
A cynical take on ambitious professionals; the moral choice is the same, the tone is far colder.

h: A bomb on a city bus will go off if it drops below 50 miles per hour; a lean, ridiculous, white-knuckle stunt-driven ride.

like.r: The model of the one-man-versus-the-terrorist action film, with more banter.
A long chase film built around a vehicle that must never stop, grander and weirder.
A decade-defining, plain chase thriller with a train crash, a bit more serious.

h: A surgeon falsely convicted of his wife's murder escapes a wreck and hunts the one-armed man while a marshal hunts him.

like.r: The original wrong-man chase thriller, wittier and more stylish.
Another innocent man hunted by powerful forces, with more surveillance gadgets.
A leaner, sillier 1990s action thriller with the same relentless forward motion.

h: A Scottish farmer turned rebel leads a bloody, mud-soaked uprising against the English; big on speeches, battles and blue face paint.

like.r: Another old-world epic of a vengeful soldier-turned-rebel, with more spectacle and gloom.
Another sweeping, sincere 1990s epic about an outsider joining a people, slower and gentler.
A historical adventure with fierce action and a soaring romance, more lyrical.

h: A banker jailed for two murders he says he did not commit befriends a lifer and holds onto hope across decades inside.

like.r: The collection that includes the original novella, with the same patient narrator and more of King's compassion.
Darabont's other long King prison drama, with a supernatural touch and more tears.
An earlier prison story of an unbreakable man who inspires others, with a harsher chain-gang setting.

h: Five criminals meet in a police lineup and are drawn into a job for a legendary boss no one has seen; a story told by a man you can't trust.

like.r: Another group of criminals thrown together and distrusting each other, rawer and more talky.
A twisty crime story with a larger, richer noir design.
A later puzzle that withholds the truth through a faulty narrator, built backwards.

h: Three mismatched 1950s LAPD cops circle a massacre and a ring of corruption in a dense, beautifully shot noir.

like.r: The sprawling novel is darker and far more tangled; the film is a tidy, gripping distillation.
The classic Los Angeles noir about a city's rot, with a sadder and more personal detective.
A later cop thriller about loyalty and betrayal on both sides of the law, louder and bloodier.

h: A San Francisco detective falls for the novelist who may have killed her lover, in a lurid, glossy erotic thriller.

like.r: The sultry neo-noir of an ordinary man lured by a dangerous woman, sweatier and better plotted.
The San Francisco classic of a detective fatally obsessed with a woman, much subtler.
Another hit about desire turned deadly, with a more domestic and moralizing view.

h: A construction worker buys a fake Mars holiday and discovers his memory may be someone else's; gory, funny and bizarre.

like.t: We Can Remember It for You Wholesale
like.r: The short story is quieter, funnier and more paranoid, with a very different ending.
Verhoeven's other violent, satirical sci-fi action film, more of a media parody.
Another Philip K. Dick adaptation about a self that can't be trusted, slower and more melancholy.

h: A convict sent back from a ruined future to stop a plague is declared insane in the past; a paranoid, tragic time-travel loop.

like.r: Another story of a messenger sent back from a ruined future, as a lean action thriller instead of a tragedy.
Gilliam's earlier dystopian fantasy, with the same bureaucratic paranoia and a more comic touch.
A later time-travel thriller with a hitman meeting himself, more action-oriented.

t: Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas
h: A journalist and his lawyer rent a convertible and a suitcase of drugs and hallucinate through Las Vegas; deranged and hilarious, with a grim underside.

like.t: Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas
like.r: The book is a wilder, more caustic piece of gonzo journalism with an angrier view of America.
Another shambling, stoned comedy of strange encounters, gentler and more plotted.
Another hallucinatory, stylized dive into excess with a charismatic narrator.

h: A cheerful insurance man slowly realizes that his whole town is a set and his life is a television show.

like.r: Another film about a too-perfect artificial town, more of a fable about change.
The classic about total surveillance, far bleaker; Truman asks the same questions with a smile.
Released the next year, with the same world-is-fake premise, as an action movie.

h: A programmer hypnotized into total apathy decides to stop caring about work, and the cubicle farm cannot cope.

like.r: Another dead-end-job comedy of slackers, cruder and shot on a shoestring.
The same year's angrier view of office-drone despair, played as violence instead of satire.

like.t: Then We Came to the End
like.r: A novel in the collective voice of an advertising office, with the same jokes and a sadder ending.

h: A bitter teacher tries to rig a high-school student council race against an overachiever he can't stand; petty, hilarious and pointed.

like.r: The short novel is told in several voices and is just as cutting about ambition and small-time politics.
A darker and more violent high-school satire.
Another film about an obsessive teenager and an adult he tangles with, quirkier and sweeter.

h: A puppeteer finds a tiny door in an office that leads inside the head of the actor John Malkovich; fifteen minutes later, you're spat out onto a highway.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: Another Charlie Kaufman script about love and identity with a surreal premise, more emotional.
The same director and writer's next film, which is even more self-referential and funnier.
Another unsettling comedy of a writer and a weird building that is hard to explain.

h: After the Gulf War, four soldiers go chasing Saddam's looted gold and discover who they are actually fighting for.

like.r: Another satire of war as absurd bureaucracy, with the same black humor.
Another Gulf War film, drier and more about waiting than fighting.
A far bigger journey into the madness of a war, with a more mythic tone.

h: A man wakes with no memory in a night-bound city where strangers rearrange the buildings at midnight, in gothic noir style.

like.r: The model for this kind of rain-dark future city and its questions about memory and humanity.
The next year's bigger blockbuster, which used some of the same ideas and sets.
The silent ancestor of dystopian cities as machines, more allegorical.

h: In a future that sorts people by their genes, a man with the wrong DNA borrows a better identity to chase the stars.

like.r: The classic of a society engineered at birth, with a colder satire.
Another future about what makes someone human, noisier and much more dystopian.
Another quiet, sorrowful look at people shaped by bioscience, with a lot more heartbreak.

h: Giant saucers park over every major city and then start blowing them up; a big, loud summer blockbuster with speeches and one-liners.

like.r: The original alien invasion novel, grim and eerie, with an unheroic narrator.

like.t: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
like.r: A more awestruck vision of a visit from above, with wonder instead of explosions.
Another Will Smith alien blockbuster, but a lighter comic fantasy.

h: A secret agency polices aliens living in New York, and a new recruit learns the job from a deadpan veteran; sleek and silly.

like.r: Another comic story of professionals who handle the paranormal in New York, with a rougher, more improvised wit.
A loving, goofier sci-fi comedy from the same period, with more heart.

like.t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
like.r: The great British comic sci-fi novel about a very ordinary man among aliens.

h: An FBI agent and a terrorist swap faces and lives, and two over-the-top performances fight through slow-motion gunfights.

like.r: Woo's Hong Kong action masterwork, with even wilder shootouts and less nonsense.
A sober cat-and-mouse crime thriller with a famous shootout, more realistic.
A glossy 1990s spy-action film with big set pieces and shifting identities.

h: An FBI rookie goes undercover with a gang of bank-robbing surfers and falls for the philosophy of their leader.

like.r: A cooler, more serious story about cops and thieves who respect each other.
The undercover-among-the-thrill-seekers formula reworked for street racing.
Bigelow's later, tense look at an adrenaline junkie, set in war.

h: Two friends on a weekend away are forced to run from the law after one terrible night, and the road liberates them.

like.r: The outlaw road movie it echoes, with a more romantic and bloody view of life on the run.
Another lyrical, doomed road trip across open country, much more detached.
A much more violent chase in which women flee a man's world to find freedom.

h: A Civil War soldier posted to a lonely frontier fort befriends the Lakota and slowly becomes one of them; wide plains, long runtime.

like.r: The novel the film is based on, with the same journey in prose, and an even closer look at the Comanche.
Another frontier epic with a romance and historical clash, with more action.
A western from the same period that questions the genre instead of celebrating the land.

h: A moon mission crippled by an explosion, told as a nail-biting puzzle for the astronauts and the engineers on the ground.

like.r: The astronaut's own account the film is based on, with more technical detail on the near-disaster.
A longer, wilder epic about the first astronauts and test pilots.
A modern, funnier problem-solving survival story in space.

h: Two young military lawyers defend Marines accused of killing a comrade, building to a shouted courtroom showdown.

like.r: The classic of tense argument in a single room, plainer and more philosophical.
A page-turning legal thriller that is also a hit of its era, more conspiratorial.
Another star-heavy courtroom drama of the era, with a more emotional personal story.

h: A novelist rescued from a snowy crash wakes up in the home of his biggest fan, who is unhappy about how his book ends.

like.r: The novel is nastier and more inward about a writer's relationship to his readers.
Another snowbound King story of isolation and a writer in trouble, creepier and more supernatural.
The immobile-hero thriller that taught everyone how to squeeze suspense out of one location.

h: A murdered banker lingers as a ghost to protect his girlfriend, aided by a fraudulent psychic; romance, comedy and thriller in one.

like.r: A quieter British story of grief and a lover who comes back as a ghost.
Another sentimental romance in which a dead man watches over the woman he loved.
A later, equally tearful romance for audiences who loved the big feelings.

h: Two cheerfully brainless friends drive a van across the country to return a briefcase, in a nonstop pileup of gags.

like.c: Jim Abrahams & David Zucker & Jerry Zucker
like.r: The original gag-per-second spoof comedy, with smarter parody and a similar innocence.
Another best-friends comedy of dumb catchphrases, more pop-culture-heavy.
A sweeter, sillier tale of two lovable idiots on a quest.

h: A man hires a private detective to find his prom date thirteen years on, and everyone who sees her falls for her; gross-out meets sweetness.

like.r: The Farrellys' earlier, dumber and less romantic comedy.
A classic, wittier and tamer romcom for a similar crowd.
A later crude-but-warm comedy with real affection beneath the jokes.

h: Two metalhead friends with a public-access show in a basement get a shot at fame, and the fourth wall gets broken constantly.

like.r: Another sweet, slangy odd-couple comedy of dim best friends who save the world.
The great mockumentary about a hair-metal band, drier and more cutting.
A more laid-back and realistic hangout comedy to a classic rock soundtrack.

t: Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery
h: A frozen 1960s spy thaws out in the 1990s with bad teeth and a libido; a giddy, catchphrase-heavy spoof of Bond and swinging London.

like.r: A 1960s spy spoof with a swaggering ladies' man hero, the kind of thing Austin Powers sends up, more straight-faced.

like.t: The Naked Gun: From the Files of Police Squad!
like.r: Another dead-serious hero and a nonstop deluge of gags, in a cop-movie parody.
One of the Bond films that is being spoofed, played straight and stylish.

h: Four high school friends make a pact to lose their virginity by prom, and the crude jokes hide a sincere streak.

like.r: A later, more verbal and equally sweet teen sex comedy about best friends.
The ancestor of rowdy campus comedies, rougher and anarchic.
A more honest and ensemble look at teenage sex and school.

h: A blocked young Shakespeare finds a muse in disguise, and Romeo and Juliet gets written in the middle of a romance and a comedy of errors.

like.r: A sunnier, Shakespeare-faithful comedy of witty lovers, more rustic.
A lavish look at a famous artist's life with a larger, more tragic scope.
Another period romance of wit and constraint with the same ensemble.

h: An FBI agent infiltrates the mob and is befriended by a low-level hit man who thinks he is a fellow thief.

like.r: A broader, more glamorous view of the same mob world, with a flashier style.
Another undercover-in-the-mob story with a divided loyalty, louder and plottier.
Another crime film with a bond between men on opposite sides of the law.

h: Two lovers kill their way across the Southwest and become media stars, in a jittery collage of film stocks and lurid satire.

like.r: The classic outlaw-lovers movie, far more romantic and restrained.
A deadpan, dreamy killing spree through the Plains, with all the lyricism Stone lacks.
Another stylized look at violence as entertainment, colder and more literary.

h: A comic-shop clerk and a call girl steal a suitcase of mob cocaine and run for Hollywood, with a Tarantino script full of sweet talk and gore.

like.r: The same writer directing his own crime comedy, bigger and more structurally daring.
Another lovers-on-the-run film from a Tarantino story, harsher and much more stylized.
A calmer, more poetic version of a young couple fleeing across the country.

h: A nun becomes spiritual adviser to a death-row killer and tries to see him as a person before the execution date.

like.r: Sister Helen's own memoir is plainer and more detailed about the cases and the victims' families.
Another death-row drama, more sentimental and fantastical in tone.
The stark black-and-white account of a real killing and its aftermath, less sympathetic.

h: A young trans man reinvents himself in small-town Nebraska and finds love, then the town finds out; tender and devastating, based on a real case.

like.r: Another film about young outsiders and identity at the edge of the American heartland, dreamier.
Another tragic love story about hiding in rural America, quieter and more lyrical.
A harrowing true-life drama about a woman failed by everyone around her.

h: A screenwriter moves to Las Vegas to drink himself to death and meets a prostitute who agrees not to stop him; a hard and painfully tender love story.

like.r: The classic novel of a drinker's last day, denser and far more literary.
A more frenzied and punishing film about addiction.
Another film about a poet drinking himself down, funnier and scruffier.

h: Three friends grow up in South Central Los Angeles under different pressures and with different fathers; a first film with a lot of anger and love.

like.r: A more stylized and politically sharp portrait of a Black neighborhood on a hot day.
Another 1990s film about growing up in a violent neighborhood, much bleaker.
A later and more lyrical coming-of-age story in a poor Black neighborhood.

h: Two lovers flee down a hallucinatory Southern highway, with Elvis songs, sudden brutality and a witch from the Wizard of Oz.

like.r: Lynch's creepier, more unsettling exploration of dark desires under a pretty small town.
Another lovers-on-the-run crime movie, with slicker comedy and less dream logic.
The Technicolor road fantasy that Lynch twists into an obscene pop-culture nightmare.

h: A jazz saxophonist receives anonymous tapes of his house, and then his life turns into another man's; a nightmare noir without an answer key.

like.r: Lynch's next noir of split identity in Hollywood, more accessible and more heartbreaking.
The classic about obsession and a woman who might be two people, more orderly.
His surreal debut, a black-and-white industrial nightmare.

h: A gentle man released from a mental hospital after a childhood killing befriends a boy, and the drawl hides something terrible.

like.r: Another Southern story seen through innocent eyes, with a gentle outcast at its heart.
A short, devastating story of a gentle, simple-minded man and his protector.
A calm, quiet Americana story of an old man's journey, warmer and with no violence.

h: A young nobody sent to bring home a rich man's son falls in love with his life and starts stealing it, in sun-soaked Italy.

like.r: The cooler, nastier novel, with a Ripley who is far more calculating and less pained.
The earlier French version of the same story, sleeker and more amoral.
Another Highsmith story of a charming predator and a weaker man, directed with suspense.

h: An IRA volunteer who guarded a hostage looks up the man's lover in London, in a thriller that becomes a stranger love story.

like.r: Jordan's historical film on the Irish rebellion, more of a conventional epic.

like.t: In the Name of the Father
like.r: Another film about the Troubles, a wrongful-conviction drama and angrier.
Another love story that crosses expectations of identity, quieter and sadder.
